posts.text:
The Great Communist IT Department: Masters of the Hard Reset

There are bad IT guys, and then there are the ones who moonlight as dictators. Each promised shiny new software, but instead of upgrades, they specialized in catastrophic data wipes. Communism in the 20th century was less an “operating system for the people” and more a ransomware virus that kept deleting files until the hard drive screamed.

And among this terrible team of “technicians,” my favourite — yes, I admit it — remains Pol Pot. (Tried to format and reinstall a country)

The All-Stars of System Failure
· Joseph Stalin (USSR Systems Admin)
 Specialty: Mass purges, forced collectivization.
 Deleted Files: ~10–20 million users.
 Method: Accused people of being “corrupted sectors” and sent them to GulagScan™ for permanent deletion.

https://t.co/ss55vVCs5r
· Mao Zedong (China’s Chief Developer)
 Specialty: The “Great Leap Forward” patch, which promised miracles but delivered famine.
 Deleted Files: ~30–45 million users.
 Method: Installed “Agriculture Cloud 2.0” with no testing. Immediate system crash.
https://t.co/6TS1ojP4cX
https://t.co/rDpLlB1ODN

· Kim Il-Sung & Successors (North Korea Tech Support)
 Specialty: Eternal “maintenance mode.”
 Deleted Files: ~1–3 million users.
 Method: Runs country on Closed Network Mode. No internet, no updates, just bugs forever.

· Mengistu Haile Mariam (Ethiopia’s Error Handler)
 Specialty: Red Terror upgrade.
 Deleted Files: ~1 million users.
 Method: Every time the system glitched, he solved it by deleting more files.

· Pol Pot (Cambodia’s IT Visionary)
 Specialty: Full wipe, no recovery partition.
 Deleted Files: ~1.7–2 million users (25% of the system).
 Method: Declared all “apps” unnecessary. Installed Year Zero OS: a version so minimalist it deleted itself.
 Why He’s My Favorite: Others pretended to upgrade their software. Pol Pot just hit DELETE ALL, proudly called it an “innovation,” and left nothing but an empty, blinking cursor.
https://t.co/jdNSsxWCbq
https://t.co/Zi6ymda0ho

Error Report: Communism OS
· Promised features: equality, efficiency, abundance.
· Actual results: famine, executions, purges, endless “Fatal Exception” errors.
· User feedback: mostly silence, because the users had been deleted.

The Arrogance of the Next Update
What makes this system truly terrifying is not just the bugs, but the arrogance of every new “programmer.” Each one looks back at the last version and says:

“Ah, it wasn’t installed correctly. They made mistakes. I’ll run it better.”

But the truth is, they don’t fix the problem — they repeat it. That’s how the death toll has already climbed past 90 million deleted files.

So the question remains: How many more files must be erased before people admit the program doesn’t do what it says on the tin?

Is there a number that finally makes people think, “Maybe this isn’t progress, maybe it’s just another system crash”? Or will every new attempt just add another line to the list of the dead?

The Final Question
The world has already endured the ultimate hard resets of Stalin, Mao, Pol Pot, and their colleagues in the Great Communist IT Department. Their legacy isn’t progress — it’s empty screens, broken systems, and millions of lives wiped like forgotten files.
Because if history has proven anything, it’s this: Communism isn’t an operating system. It’s a virus. And every time it’s reinstalled, it wipes the drive clean.
